key_insight: A metallic glass under cyclic loading shows one unified dynamic scaling law, but the dominant energy-injection mechanism switches from macroscopic plastic work above yield to localized elastic stress fluctuations below yield.
engineering_relevance: This gives a predictive framework for tuning aging versus rejuvenation in amorphous structural and energy materials by controlling loading rate, amplitude, and cyclic stress state.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of a cyclically driven metallic glass
Compare sub-yield aging and over-yield rejuvenation across loading regimes
Extract scaling relations between relaxation behavior, plastic work, and stress fluctuations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an exact scaling identity linking the relaxation attenuation exponent to the stress fluctuation exponent, supported by observed universal dynamic scaling across both regimes.
watch_item: Because the conclusions come from molecular dynamics of one metallic glass model, transferability to other chemistries, temperatures, and experimental loading conditions still needs validation.
paper_title: Universal Dynamic Scaling for Sub-Yield Aging and Over-Yield Rejuvenation in A Cyclically Driven Metallic Glass
